question: Does separating who the lead is (Persona) from what the lead needs (Search Need) improve future prioritization relative to a single Lead profile?
hypothesis: Lead Persona and Search Need are more interpretable and improve future average precision and top-decile lift when modeled separately with Spot and Broker profiles.
primary_change: Replace the single Lead profile with two unsupervised facets: Lead Persona and Search Need.

target.censoring: The public data has no visit timestamp; the recorded inquiry response is treated as the observed proxy outcome and this limitation is reported.

population.eligibility: Inquiries after a frozen early profile-calibration window; the final 20% by inquiry_at is held out for future evaluation.
exclusions: The first 30% of inquiries are reserved only for unsupervised profile calibration and are not used to fit the predictive models.

validation.split_description: First 30% of inquiries calibrate/freeze unsupervised profiles; next 50% train the predictive model; final 20% are an untouched future test.

items.source: leads.user_type, company_size, industry, source and prior-history fields
items.evidence: All fields are part of the lead record and the clusterer is fitted/frozen in the early calibration window.

items.source: leads search sector, modality, area, budget and preferred geography
items.evidence: These are lead-declared search requirements known before the inquiry.

items.source: derived from reviewed Persona, Search Need, Spot and Broker profiles
items.evidence: No post-inquiry response information is introduced.
